sections.title: Addition Basics
sections.content:
📝 Unit 1: Addition

What is Addition?

Addition means combining numbers to find out how many you have altogether. It's like putting groups together!

🔑 Key Symbols:

The + sign means "plus" or "add"

The = sign means "equals" or "makes"

Example:

3 + 2 = 5

Read as: "Three plus two equals five"

📊 Number Range:

Single-digit addition uses numbers 0-9. The answer can be up to 18 (9+9).

💡 Quick Tip:

Start with the bigger number and count up! For 3+5, start at 5 and count: 6, 7, 8!

sections.title: Addition Example
sections.content:
Visual Addition: 4 + 3

Let's see how 4 stars plus 3 stars equals 7 stars!

First group: 4 stars

+

Plus (add them together)

Second group: 3 stars

=

Equals (the total)

Total: 7 stars

✅ Remember:

4 + 3 = 7 because when we combine 4 items and 3 items, we get 7 items total!

sections.title: Subtraction Basics
sections.content:
📝 Unit 2: Subtraction

What is Subtraction?

Subtraction means taking away or finding the difference between numbers. It's the opposite of addition!

🔑 Key Symbol:

The − sign means "minus" or "subtract"

Example:

8 − 3 = 5

Read as: "Eight minus three equals five"

📊 Important Words:

Minuend: The number you start with (8)
Subtrahend: The number you take away (3)
Difference: The answer (5)

💡 Quick Tip:

Count backwards! For 8−3, start at 8 and count back: 7, 6, 5!

🔄 Subtraction & Addition:

They're opposites! If 8 − 3 = 5, then 5 + 3 = 8

sections.title: Subtraction Example
sections.content:
Visual Subtraction: 7 − 2

Watch how we take away 2 hearts from 7 hearts!

Start with: 7 hearts

−

Minus (take away)

Take away: 2 hearts

=

Equals (what's left)

Remaining: 5 hearts

✅ Remember:

7 − 2 = 5 because when we take away 2 from 7, we have 5 left!

sections.title: Multiplication Basics
sections.content:
📝 Unit 3: Multiplication

What is Multiplication?

Multiplication is repeated addition! Instead of adding the same number many times, we can multiply!

🔑 Key Symbol:

The × sign means "times" or "multiply"

Example:

3 × 4 = 12

Read as: "Three times four equals twelve"

This means: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 (three groups of 4)

📊 Understanding:

3 × 4 means "3 groups of 4" or "4 added 3 times"

💡 Quick Tip:

Learn your times tables! Start with 1, 2, 5, and 10 — they're the easiest!

🌟 Special Rules:

• Any number × 0 = 0

• Any number × 1 = that same number

• 3 × 4 = 4 × 3 (order doesn't matter!)

sections.title: Multiplication Example
sections.content:
Visual Multiplication: 3 × 2

Let's see 3 groups of 2 cookies!

Group 1: 2 cookies

+

Group 2: 2 cookies

+

✅ Remember:

3 × 2 = 6 because we have 3 groups with 2 in each group!

This is the same as: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6

sections.title: Division Basics
sections.content:
📝 Unit 4: Division

What is Division?

Division means splitting into equal groups or sharing equally. It's the opposite of multiplication!

🔑 Key Symbol:

The ÷ sign means "divided by"

Example:

12 ÷ 3 = 4

Read as: "Twelve divided by three equals four"

This means: Split 12 into 3 equal groups = 4 in each group

📊 Two Ways to Think:

12 ÷ 3 can mean:
• 12 split into 3 groups
• How many 3s are in 12?

💡 Quick Tip:

Use multiplication to check! If 12 ÷ 3 = 4, then 4 × 3 should equal 12!

🌟 Special Rules:

• Any number ÷ 1 = that same number

• Any number ÷ itself = 1

• 0 ÷ any number = 0

sections.title: Division Example
sections.content:

Let's share 6 apples equally between 2 friends!

Start with: 6 apples to share

÷ 2

Divide between 2 friends

Friend 1 gets:

validation.hint: Think: 2 times what number equals 8? Or count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8 — that's 4 groups of 2!

sections.title: Mixed Operations Challenge
sections.content:
🎯 Final Challenge: Mixed Operations!

Solve this word problem:

Tom has 3 bags with 4 candies in each bag. He eats 4 candies. Then he shares the remaining candies equally with his friend. How many candies does each person get?

💭 Step by step:

  • Step 1: Find total candies (multiplication)
  • Step 2: Subtract candies eaten (subtraction)
  • Step 3: Share between 2 people (division)

🧮 Work it out:

• Total candies: 3 × 4 = __

• After eating: __ − 4 = __

• Each person gets: __ ÷ 2 = __

validation.successMessage: 🎉 Amazing! You're a math superstar! Here's the solution: (1) 3 × 4 = 12 total candies, (2) 12 − 4 = 8 candies left, (3) 8 ÷ 2 = 4 candies each. You used all four operations perfectly!
validation.hint: First multiply to find total candies (3 × 4). Then subtract the candies eaten (− 4). Finally, divide what's left by 2 to share equally.
